details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- agents.md:148-159 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The stable BEHAVIOURAL_SMOKE log-prefix contract is duplicated across two overlapping blocks, and the second block omits BEHAVIOURAL_SMOKE_PRESENT_INCONCLUSIVE.
  WHY: Duplicate registry entries make the downstream contract ambiguous and can cause consumers to match or classify markers inconsistently.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:189 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: SHELL_REENTRY_COMMANDS omits csh and tcsh.
  WHY: Those interpreters accept -c and can execute arbitrary commands through the shell-reentry path, so validation can be bypassed.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:615-668 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: validate_command does not recurse into nohup, nice, or setsid.
  WHY: Those passthrough commands can wrap a nested shell command that is never revalidated, letting shell re-entry bypass the guard.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:619-621 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The `$` check in validate_command rejects literal command tokens that contain a dollar sign after tokenization, including single-quoted or escaped-literal forms.
  WHY: The tokenizer strips quoting and escapes before validation, so safe literal command names can be falsely rejected.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:553-668 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: validate_command only inspects the command token and does not scan argument tokens for variable expansion.
  WHY: Inputs like echo $UNSAFE_VAR can still be expanded by the shell even though the command name itself passed validation.
- tests/test_review_reject_verify.py:832-853 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The regression test checks marker presence but not uniqueness, so duplicate entries in agents.md are not detected.
  WHY: The current assertion pattern allows repeated markers to pass, giving false confidence that the contract is clean.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:243-271 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: Moving shell-validation failures out of normalize_content changed the emitted diagnostic contract away from body_unsafe_shell_construct.
  WHY: External tooling that keys off that sentinel will stop matching because failures now surface through different validator messages.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:238-246 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: strip_outer_code_fence only removes a single outer fence and does not handle nested or unterminated code fences.
  WHY: Malformed Markdown can leave literal backticks or truncated content that breaks the generated wrapper.
- tests/test_review_synthesise_smoke.py:400-495 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The hello_hash_eval test expects eval rejection even though strip_comments removes the `;eval` fragment as a shell comment.
  WHY: With the new comment-stripping semantics, that input no longer reaches the validator with eval present, so the expected diagnostic does not occur.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:259-267, 1039-1047 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: prefer_generated_item_error can leave stderr reporting less structured plain exceptions when normalization fails outside GeneratedItemValidationError.
  WHY: The aggregation logic prefers the first higher-priority error, so some failures surface with a less informative diagnostic contract.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:617-662 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: validate_command does not block perl, ruby, or php in its dangerous-command checks.
  WHY: Those interpreters support flags that execute inline code, so generated wrappers can run arbitrary commands without tripping the validator.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- agents.md:156-159 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The stable log-prefix contract lists the same four BEHAVIOURAL_SMOKE markers twice, with the duplicate block missing BEHAVIOURAL_SMOKE_PRESENT_INCONCLUSIVE.
  WHY: Downstream log-analysis tooling will see ambiguous duplicate entries, and a consumer that picks up the legacy copy will misclassify BEHAVIOURAL_SMOKE_PRESENT_INCONCLUSIVE events.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- agents.md:148-152 and 156-159 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The stable behavioural-smoke log-prefix contract lists the same markers twice.
  WHY: Duplicate registry entries create ambiguity for downstream consumers that rely on these prefixes and create a maintenance hazard if one copy is updated independently.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:189 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: SHELL_REENTRY_COMMANDS omits csh and tcsh.
  WHY: Generated content containing csh -c or tcsh -c would bypass shell re-entry validation and execute arbitrary commands through these interpreters.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:617-663 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: validate_command does not recurse into nohup, nice, or setsid.
  WHY: Generated content like nohup bash -c "..." or nice bash -c "..." would pass validation because those commands are not handled recursively.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:620 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: validate_command falsely rejects literal command tokens containing '$' after tokenization, including single-quoted literals like '$cmd'.
  WHY: Safe literal command names containing $ in single quotes would be incorrectly rejected as unsafe variable expansion.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:553-668 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: validate_command only checks for '$' in command position and still allows variable expansion in arguments such as echo $UNSAFE_VAR.
  WHY: Generated wrapper content like echo $MALICIOUS_INPUT would pass validation because only the command position is checked.
- tests/test_review_reject_verify.py:~835 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The regression test checks that each marker is present using in but does not verify that each appears only once.
  WHY: The duplicate contract entries in agents.md therefore pass undetected because the test only confirms presence, not uniqueness.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:243-254 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Moving shell-validation failures out of normalize_content() changes the diagnostic contract from body_unsafe_shell_construct to later validator messages.
  WHY: External tooling or grep-based monitoring that looks for body_unsafe_shell_construct in logs will stop matching because the rejection now emits different diagnostic messages.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- agents.md:148-152 and 156-159 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The stable log-prefix contract lists BEHAVIOURAL_SMOKE_* markers twice, once in the primary list and again in a duplicate section that omits INCONCLUSIVE.
  WHY: Downstream log analysis consumers that rely on the stable prefix registry may encounter ambiguous or inconsistent entries, breaking the contract's stability guarantee.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:189 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: SHELL_REENTRY_COMMANDS = {'bash', 'sh', 'dash', 'ksh', 'zsh'} omits csh and tcsh.
  WHY: These interpreters can execute arbitrary commands via -c just like the listed shells, so csh -c or tcsh -c would bypass the shell re-entry validation.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:615-663 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: validate_command handles env, exec, command, builtin, time, and timeout by recursing into their nested commands, but does not handle nohup, nice, or setsid.
  WHY: Generated content like nohup bash -c '...' or setsid sh -c '...' would pass the validator because the nested command is never inspected.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:619-620 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The dollar-sign check is applied to the raw command token after tokenization has stripped quote characters, so literal command forms like '$cmd' or escaped-dollar forms like \$cmd are rejected.
  WHY: Legitimate generated content that intentionally quotes a literal dollar-sign in command position is falsely rejected, reducing synthesis success rates unnecessarily.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:238-246 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: strip_outer_code_fence only strips a single outer fence and does not handle nested or unterminated code fences.
  WHY: Markdown content with inner ``` markers or a missing closing fence can leave literal backticks or mangled content in the generated wrapper, which can break execution.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:252-271 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The old diagnostic contract value "body_unsafe_shell_construct" is no longer raised by normalize_content(); validation failures now come from validate_shell_content() with different error messages.
  WHY: External tooling that greps for the old sentinel will stop matching, which is a breaking change to the diagnostic contract.
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
- agents.md:148-152 and lines 156-159 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Four stable log-prefix markers appear twice in the stable log prefixes contract, with the block added by this PR duplicating entries that already existed at lines 156-159.
  WHY: Downstream log-analysis tooling keyed off this contract may double-count or mis-classify these markers, and the test only checks presence so it does not catch the duplication.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:619-668 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The dollar-sign check in validate_command is applied after tokenization strips quote characters, so quoted literal commands like '$cmd' or escaped-dollar forms like \$cmd are rejected even though the shell treats them as literals.
  WHY: Legitimate generated content that intentionally quotes a literal dollar-sign in command position is falsely rejected, reducing synthesis success rates unnecessarily.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:619-668 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: validate_command recursively validates nested commands for env, exec, command, builtin, time, and timeout, but does NOT recurse into nohup, nice, or setsid.
  WHY: A generated item containing nohup bash -c '...' or setsid sh -c '...' would pass the validator and then be executed from the synthesised wrapper heredoc, defeating the shell-re-entry guard.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:189 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: csh and tcsh are absent from the shell-re-entry command allowlist.
  WHY: csh -c '...' or tcsh -c '...' would pass validation and then execute an arbitrary command, bypassing the shell-re-entry guard.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:619-668 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: validate_command only rejects '$' in the command token and still allows variable expansion in argument tokens.
  WHY: Generated wrapper content like echo $MALICIOUS_INPUT would pass validation because only the command position is checked, allowing shell expansion at runtime.
- tests/test_review_synthesise_smoke.py:400-495 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The hello_hash_eval test expects eval rejection even though strip_comments removes the `;eval` fragment as a shell comment.
  WHY: With the new strip_comments semantics, that specific input no longer reaches validation with eval present, so the asserted diagnostic does not appear.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:259-267 and 1039-1047 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: prefer_generate
